title: T1030 — Data Transfer Size Limits
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Data Transfer Size Limits with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: The export is collected
steps.caption: The implant on the database host DB-APP-07 receives a task and runs a full dump of the customers table. The result is a single 60 MB export file in a temp folder. EDR shows a large mysqldump child process on DB-APP-07 writing to a temp path
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

fields.detail: The implant on the database host DB-APP-07 receives a task and runs a full dump of the customers tab

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: The alarm line is measured
steps.caption: The operator checks the victim's controls and finds the line: the egress DLP gateway raises an alert for uploads over 10 MB. A public policy page and a misconfigured console had already exposed the limit. one probe upload of 11 MB fired an alert that nobody joined to the recon session
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

detection.label: No detection

steps.title: The archive is split
steps.caption: The implant packs the export into an encrypted archive and splits it into 9 MB volumes. One smaller final part completes the set, and every part sits under the line. Sysmon records 7z started with a -v9m volume flag, then part files appearing in temp
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Part 1 slips through
steps.caption: The first 9 MB part uploads to the attacker's cloud bucket. It is under the line, so the gateway stays silent. the proxy records one 9 MB POST to a brand-new external host - below every threshold, no rule fires
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: The streak builds
steps.caption: Parts 2 to 6 follow over the next hours. Every part is the same size, from the same host, to the same bucket. each upload is still under the line. Only the counters note the repetition: same size, same host, six times
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.caption: Part 7 carries the final 6 MB. It uploads next to a small README that describes how the parts fit together. The streak is complete: 60 MB total. the upload streak counter reaches seven parts - 60 MB in six hours from one host to one destination

steps.title: Reassembly on the far side
steps.caption: The attacker joins the parts back into the original archive and deletes them from the bucket. No stolen file ever moved in one piece. bucket activity shows a rapid download of all parts, then deletion - the theft is already finished
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

detection.label: Alert raised
detection.detail: The SOC has enough evidence to open an incident.

steps.title: The aggregate screams
steps.caption: A streak alert fires: six uploads of near-identical size plus one smaller final part, one new destination, within six hours. The SOC blocks the bucket and isolates DB-APP-07. aggregate analytics did what per-upload rules could not - they turned seven silent uploads into one loud pattern
